content.intro: This lesson develops topic 214 of the supplied curriculum: **Sensor and Time-Series Data**. The main starting point is **Organizing sampled measurements**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: An analysis workflow is a chain of explicit stages: validate input, clean data, apply numerical operations, summarize results, and save enough metadata to reproduce the output.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Sensor and Time-Series Data** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Organizing sampled measurements** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

times = np.arange('2026-10-01', '2026-10-04', dtype='datetime64[D]')
readings = np.array([20.1, 20.5, 19.9])
print(times.shape, readings.mean().round(2))
